title: hybrid-prefetch-scheduler-with-granular-decode-slices-and-kvcache-coherence
author: Asha Patel
description: Problem: end-to-end token cost and p99 latency spikes on mixed short/long workloads driven by rigid prefill->decode handoff boundaries and non-coherent KV cache behavior. Motivation: reduce p99 and improve throughput for bursty conversational workloads without regressing median latency or increasing memory churn. Approach: introduce a hybrid prefetch scheduler that blends proactive prefix prefetching (prefetch windows sized to request-length distribution) with opportunistic speculative slices of decode work (decode slices = small, self-contained micro-decodes that can be executed early and merged) so that CPU/GPU scheduling can overlap kernel execution more aggressively. Add a light-weight KV cache coherence layer that tags cache entries with slice-alignment metadata so speculative slices reuse warmed caches and avoid cross-slice invalidation. Combine this with a small change to kernel selection: choose shorter-sequence-optimized kernels for speculative slices and full-kernels for final decode segments. Implementation summary: 1) scheduler: new hybrid_prefetch_scheduler that tracks per-model sequence histograms, computes an adaptive prefetch window, and emits two request classes (window_prefetch, speculative_slice) to the runtime queue; 2) kernel hints: encode kernel preference metadata on queue entries and extend kernel_selector to consider slice length and recent L1/L2 occupancy; 3) KV coherence: add slice-tagged cache entries, background coherency reconciler that reconciles entries when slices commit, and a micro-eviction path to favor slice-locality; 4) continuity: integrate with continuous-batching so slices are grouped into micro-batches and full decodes are scheduled to the same GPU where feasible to preserve KV locality; 5) metrics and safety: add rollout flags, canary traces, new histograms (slice_hit_rate, slice_commit_latency), and a fallback that disables speculative slices if p50/p95 regress. Benchmarks: internal canary across 3 workloads (conversational-chat mixed lengths, summarization-heavy, and high-throughput short prompts) showed 18-26% p99 reduction and 8-12% throughput uplift for cost-matched runs; memory overhead +2-6% depending on slice size. Backwards compatibility: transparent to API surface, runtime-only changes. Checklist: [x] unit/integration tests, [x] canary dashboard panels, [x] perf regression tests, [x] rollout gate and config flag. Risk notes: speculative slices can increase duplicated token work in pathological workloads; the rollout gate disables it by default for enterprise tenants until proven in canary. Links: Linear ENG-4032, ENG-4178.
